gates.description: Baseline metrics (p50, p95, p99 latency; throughput; error rate) must be captured before any optimization
Load test must be executed at 2x expected peak traffic — not just at current load
N+1 query patterns must be identified and eliminated — batch queries, JOINs, or DataLoader pattern
Every cache must have TTL, invalidation trigger, and stale behavior defined — no undefined caching
p99 latency must be within SLA — tail latency is not acceptable to ignore
Services must be stateless (no local file storage, no sticky sessions) to enable horizontal scaling

anti_patterns.description: Optimizing code that runs once per request for nanosecond improvements — profile first, optimize measured bottlenecks
'We'll cache it' without defining when the cache becomes stale — caches without invalidation are bugs with a delay
Adding more services to 'scale' while introducing network latency between them — if service calls add >50% overhead, consolidate
Fetching a list then querying for each item individually — the #1 performance killer in data-heavy applications
Upgrading to a bigger instance every time performance degrades — horizontal scaling is cheaper and more resilient
p50 is fine but p99 is 10x worse — 'most users are happy' ignores 1% who aren't

escalation_triggers: System cannot meet SLA at current architecture — requires redesign
Performance regression detected that cannot be traced to a specific change
Database approaching storage/connection limits with no clear optimization path
Third-party service latency is the dominant bottleneck and they have no SLA improvement
Cost of scaling exceeds budget by >50% and optimization alone is insufficient
Performance fix requires a breaking change to a public API

input_requirements.description: Spec.md with performance SLAs and current load profile

output_certifications: Baseline metrics captured (p50, p95, p99, throughput, error rate) before optimization
Load test executed at 2x expected peak traffic
N+1 query patterns identified and eliminated
Every cache has TTL, invalidation trigger, and stale behavior defined
Services are stateless — horizontal scaling enabled
